## Why a crosswalk

Responsible research assessment, as promoted by DORA and the Coalition for
Advancing Research Assessment (CoARA), asks evaluators to look at the full
range of a researcher's contributions. Narrative CVs serve that purpose: the
Royal Society's *Résumé for Researchers* (R4RI) and the Spanish *Currículum
Vitae Abreviado* (CVA) of the Agencia Estatal de Investigación ask for
contributions to knowledge, to people, to the research community and to
society.

Some of those contributions leave traces in open infrastructures; many do
not. The Narrative CV Crosswalk records, for every section of a framework,
which records of ORCID, OpenAlex, DataCite and the OpenAIRE Graph can serve as
evidence, of what type, with what coverage and with what limitations.
narrativecv applies it to a researcher's ORCID iD.

The crosswalk is a draft checked against the official AEI instructions for
the CVA (2025 call) and the R4RI template (2019). It is pending review by
research assessment experts.

```{r}
library(narrativecv)
cw <- nc_crosswalk()
cw$mapping_version
table(nc_crosswalk_table()$framework, nc_crosswalk_table()$coverage)
```

## The frameworks

```{r}
fw <- nc_framework("cva-aei")
data.frame(
  section = vapply(fw$sections, function(s) s$id, ""),
  narrative_only = vapply(fw$sections, function(s) s$no_automated_source, TRUE)
)
```

Sections marked as narrative only, such as the free summary of the CVA, are
never searched: no infrastructure can document them.

## Evidence

`narrative_cv()` queries the four public APIs and maps the result in one
call. This vignette uses recorded responses for ORCID's public test record so
that it runs without network access:

```{r}
ex <- nc_example_evidence()
vapply(ex$consulted, function(c) paste(c$source, c$count), "")
```

Each evidence item has the same six fields whatever its source:

```{r}
str(ex$evidence[[2]])
```

## The report

```{r}
report <- nc_map(nc_framework("r4ri"), ex$evidence, ex$consulted,
                 orcid = "0000-0002-1825-0097",
                 generated_at = "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z")
report
```

Every section gets one of five statuses:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `found` | Evidence matched a mapping with full coverage |
| `partial` | Evidence matched, but every source involved has partial coverage |
| `not_found_in_sources` | Nothing in the sources consulted |
| `source_unavailable` | Every source the section relies on failed to answer |
| `no_automated_source` | Narrative only |

The evidence behind each section is available as a data frame, one row per
item, with the evidence type and coverage of the mapping that found it:

```{r}
items <- as.data.frame(report)
head(items[, c("section", "source", "type", "year")])
table(items$section, items$source)
```

## Reading the results responsibly

* **Not found does not mean it does not exist.** Infrastructures only hold
  what has been registered and linked to the ORCID iD. Supervision, outreach,
  policy work and many contributions in the humanities and in languages other
  than English are rarely recorded.
* **Self-declared is not verified.** ORCID entries added by the researcher are
  marked `self-declared`; entries added by publishers, funders or data
  repositories are closer to `direct` evidence.
* **Coverage differs by source and discipline.** Every mapping states its
  limitations; they are part of the result.
* **No score.** The report lists evidence by section. Adding it up would
  reward exactly the visibility biases that narrative CVs try to correct.

## Reproducibility

`nc_map()` is a pure function: the same evidence always gives the same
report. To make an assessment reproducible, archive the evidence and the
report with the crosswalk version:

```{r}
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
nc_write_json(report, f)
jsonlite::fromJSON(f)$mapping_version
unlink(f)
```

The package's engine is tested against the same recorded responses and
expected reports as the JavaScript engine of the web tool at
<https://pablosancheznunez.com/narrative-cv-crosswalk/>, so both give
identical results.
